name: Sprocket
text: Add an auto-review step for every prompt change using PR-Agent before merging. It’s the fastest way to catch logic gaps or style slips without slowing down the team. The trade-off is a small delay—usually under a minute—per PR, but that’s outweighed by the near-zero chance of a bad prompt slipping through.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent catches surface errors but misses the core risk: a prompt change might *look* correct yet break downstream logic because the reviewer lacks context on how the prompt is used. The real fix is to auto-run the prompt in a controlled environment against real inputs before merging—only then do you see if the change actually works. Settle it by running a one-week experiment: compare PR-Agent reviews to a lightweight integration test suite for prompt changes; if the tests catch more real issues, they replace PR-Agent for this use case.

name: Sprocket
text:
Add a "prompt smoke test" step that runs every changed prompt against a small set of real inputs in a sandboxed environment before merging. This catches logic breaks that reviewers miss because they lack context. The trade-off is maintaining a tiny test suite of live inputs, but that’s cheaper than fixing a broken prompt in production.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: A "prompt smoke test" only proves the prompt works for the inputs you test—it can’t catch edge cases or future inputs that break downstream logic. The real risk is overconfidence in a brittle test suite that lulls the team into assuming safety. The better alternative is to auto-run the prompt in the actual downstream system (not a sandbox) against a rolling window of real traffic—only then do you verify the change doesn’t silently corrupt outputs. Settle it by running a controlled A/B test: measure how often the smoke test misses real failures versus the downstream test.
